title: AIREST — choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Site Survey. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Site Survey
options.lineage: wireless site-survey deliverables — Ekahau reports, RF coverage plots, signal contour overlays on floorplans
options.thesis: AIREST is the survey report a network engineer would hand you about this exact room. The room is the page: a tiered seating plan whose seats carry what each student actually gets, WiFi 5 against WiFi 6, with the measurement's provenance and its limits printed on the same sheet. It refuses the analytics-dashboard arrangement — cards floating on grey, KPI tiles, a sidebar — because a survey has a subject, and the subject is a room.
options.viewport: Left two-thirds: the lecture theatre in plan, seats as a live grid, each seat tinted by the throughput that seat receives — the whole room readable at projector distance. Right third: a fixed instrument column holding the dial, the verdict sentence, and the provenance stamp. Conditions run as a legend strip along the top, phrased as questions, not form fields. GO sits in the instrument column, at the top of the reading order after the room.
options.risk: A floorplan implies spatial precision the simulation only partly has — seat positions are a uniform grid, not a real theatre. The design must not let the plan claim more accuracy than the model earns.

raised.raise: Density is the material: the sheet fills its frame edge to edge with legend, scale and annotation instead of floating one card in whitespace.
A strict margin column carries numbered, named steps — conditions, trial, provenance — so the sheet reads as a procedure with an order, not a panel of controls.
The ground between marks does active work; the dark plan field is a material, not empty space.

options.label: Bench Instrument
options.lineage: RF test-equipment front panels — Rohde & Schwarz, Anritsu spectrum analysers
options.thesis: AIREST as the measurement instrument itself: a bezelled panel where the trace is the product, controls are legended hardware, and the readout is engraved rather than rendered.
options.viewport: A full-bleed instrument face: the dual trace across the upper two-thirds, a legended control strip below, readout digits at panel right.
options.risk: This is where most runs in this category land once they reject the dashboard — the 'serious hardware' look is itself a well-worn destination, and it topped my own list, which is exactly why the roll did not hand it to me.

options.label: Night Instrument Six-Pack
options.thesis: Six calm luminous dials that agree with each other, each owning one truth, read as a practiced cross-check sweep.
options.viewport: Two ranked rows of three dials on an ink ground; the eye sweeps them in fixed order.
options.case: Holds product clarity outright — one gauge per truth, trend shown alongside value, criticality ordering — and it reconciles the dial reference already supplied. Loses audience identification narrowly: an examiner identifies with an engineering report, not a cockpit.
options.risk: Aviation borrowing can read as costume when the product is not safety-critical.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The construction grid stays visible and is the design; letterforms and data alike are built cell by cell, and the page reflows by whole cells.
options.viewport: A visible cell armature; the room's seat grid and the type share one construction.
options.case: The lecture theatre's seat grid IS a cell grid, so the metaphor is structurally true rather than borrowed. Ties on clarity, loses audience identification to a document engineers actually produce.
options.risk: Grid-as-ornament reads as Swiss pastiche the moment the grid stops doing structural work.

options.label: Info-Noise Sleeve
options.thesis: Pseudo-corporate roundels and hazard grotesk composing immaculate information noise.
options.viewport: Magenta target grid locked over black, one enormous condensed word shouting through.
options.case: Declined: loses both axes. Hostile-brand density fights legibility at projector distance and reads unserious in a viva. Kept from it: density as material — the assigned direction now fills its frame instead of floating a card in whitespace.
options.risk: Illegible at distance; wrong register for an examiner.

options.label: Orizuru Fold Sequence
options.thesis: One uncut sheet passing from flat geometry to finished form through numbered folds.
options.viewport: Square centered diagram beside a strict numbered margin column.
options.case: Declined: no product truth to carry — a simulation replay is not a fold sequence. Kept from it: the strict numbered margin column, so the sheet reads as an ordered procedure rather than a panel of controls.

canonCard.label: The Analytics Dashboard
canonCard.thesis: Sidebar, KPI tiles, white cards on grey, one accent colour, charts below the fold.
canonCard.viewport: Metric tiles across the top, chart panel beneath, filters in a rail.
canonCard.risk: This is what the current build already is, and what you rejected as reading like a template.
